title: Give an example of Solace's hierarchical routing: a news system publishes to `ps/news/{type}/{country}/{city}`, and consumers subscribe with patterns like `ps/news/*/BR/>` (all news from Brazil, any type, any city) or `ps/news/SPORT/>` (all sport news): and why is this hard to do in Kafka (you need separate topics per combination, or consumer-side filtering, or a stream processing layer)?
shortTitle: Give an example of Solace's hierarchical routing: publishing to `ps/news/{type}/{country}/{city}` and subscribing with patterns like `ps/news/*/BR/>` or `ps/news/SPORT/>`: and why is this hard in Kafka?
keyPoints: Solace topics are hierarchical strings like txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large, not pre-created broker objects.
The single-level wildcard (*) matches exactly one level; the multi-level wildcard (>) matches one or more remaining levels.
The Solace broker evaluates every message against active subscriptions and delivers only matches.
In Kafka, a topic is a flat pre-created log and the broker does no content-based routing.
Reproducing Solace routing in Kafka requires many fine-grained topics, consumer-side filtering, or a stream-processing layer.
Each Kafka workaround has a cost: topic explosion, wasted network bandwidth, or extra infrastructure.
The Solace broker uses a trie-based matcher for near-constant matching time per topic level.

s1_definition.oneliner: In Solace the broker is smart and routes each message by its hierarchical topic pattern; in Kafka the broker is simple and the consumer must do the filtering itself.
s1_definition.profdef:
Solace hierarchical routing lets a publisher encode routing dimensions directly into a slash-separated topic string, and subscribers use wildcards to express interest.

- **Hierarchical topic** – a publish-time string like `txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large` where each level carries one routing dimension.
- **Single-level wildcard (*)** – matches exactly one level, so `txn/*/Mumbai/>` matches any country with Mumbai as the city.
- **Multi-level wildcard (>)** – matches one or more remaining levels at the end, so `txn/IN/>` matches everything under India.
- **Broker-side matching** – the Solace broker evaluates all subscriptions per message and delivers only to matching consumers.
- **Kafka flat topic** – a pre-created partitioned log where the broker delivers all records to the consumer with no filtering.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India has a single pneumatic tube network for transaction alerts. Every alert is labelled with a structured address: country, city, account type, and size. Each desk tells the mailroom a pattern: "send me anything from India, Mumbai, any type" or "send me all large savings from any city." The mailroom reads each label and routes the alert only to the matching desks. Nobody receives alerts they did not ask for, and adding a new desk is just registering a new pattern. In Kafka, every desk gets every alert and sorts through the pile themselves.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Solace Hierarchical Routing Example:

  Published Topics:
  txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large
  txn/IN/Delhi/current/small
  txn/BR/SaoPaulo/savings/medium
        │
        ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │     Solace Broker         │
  │     (trie matcher)        │
  │                           │
  │  Active Subscriptions:    │
  │  Priya:  txn/IN/>         │──► Priya receives:
  │  Pankaj: txn/IN/*/sav/lg  │    txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large
  │  Rajesh: txn/BR/>         │    txn/IN/Delhi/current/small
  └──────────────────────────┘
        │            │
        │            └──► Pankaj receives:
        │                 txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large
        │
        └──► Rajesh receives:
             txn/BR/SaoPaulo/savings/medium

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────

  Same scenario in Kafka:

  Option 1: 450 topics          Option 2: 1 topic
  txn.in.mumbai.savings.large   bank.transactions
  txn.in.mumbai.savings.small     │
  txn.in.delhi.current.small      ├─ Consumer A: reads ALL, filters
  ... (450 total)                 ├─ Consumer B: reads ALL, filters
  Operational nightmare.          └─ Consumer C: reads ALL, filters
                                  Wasted bandwidth.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Solace hierarchical routing lets a publisher encode routing dimensions directly into a slash-separated topic string, and subscribers express interest with level-aware wildcards. The single-level wildcard `*` matches exactly one level, so `txn/IN/*/savings/large` matches any city in India with large savings. The multi-level wildcard `>` matches one or more remaining levels, so `txn/IN/>` matches everything from India at any depth. The broker evaluates every message against all active subscriptions using a trie-based matcher and delivers only matching messages.

This is hard to reproduce in Kafka because Kafka's broker is deliberately simple. A topic is a flat, pre-created, partitioned log, the broker does no content-based routing, and a consumer reads every record in its assigned partitions. To get Solace-like behavior in Kafka you need many fine-grained topics (which explodes topic count), consumer-side filtering (which wastes bandwidth), or a stream-processing layer (which adds infrastructure).

At National Bank of India, Priya subscribed to `txn/IN/>` and received all India transactions. Pankaj subscribed to `txn/IN/*/savings/large` and received only large savings across all Indian cities. A single Mumbai large savings event matched both subscriptions and was delivered to both. Adding a new desk was just registering a new subscription pattern, with no topics to create and no producer to modify.

Remember one sentence: Solace's broker matches each message's hierarchical topic against wildcard subscriptions and delivers only to interested consumers, while Kafka delivers everything and expects consumers to filter on their own.
